rows.what the ink shows: The faint upper pencil annotation has a long descending first stroke and several very pale short strokes to its right. Enlargement and added contrast do not separate a reliable c and crossed t from the paper texture.

The sloping pencil word has a looped descending stroke toward its left and an ascending/crossing stroke near its right. The intervening pale marks and any accent or i dots remain too indistinct to establish the complete word.

The lower pencil word to the left of the K formula has a short rising/descending s stroke, a joined shallow u, and a long rightward terminal r stroke; rotation makes this short sequence separable from the formula.

A heavy horizontal deletion passes through the entire phrase after M. A descending u-like stroke survives near the beginning, several linked lower humps survive in the middle, and an acute accent survives above the right end; the individual letters of all three words are not recoverable under the strike and the inserted formula.

The opening parenthesis survives as a curved upright immediately before the low linked letter humps. The deletion covers the body and connections of the word, so the full sequence mesure is plausible but not independently distinguishable.
The single deleted symbol after sur has two slanting uprights but is crossed by several thick oblique and horizontal strokes; the middle needed to establish M is masked.

Inside the parentheses after K superscript infinity, the inserted capital I is dark and clear. A separate oblique remnant is visible at its lower left, but the older symbol is covered by the thick I stem and lower bar.
The crossed phrase begins with an open-bow capital P and then a low e/s sequence ending in an upright crossed t. The deletion lies low enough that the P bowl and final t remain visible.

The formula has the infinity mark above and a small K below the main letter; inside the parentheses the argument has a tall left stroke and two diverging diagonal arms, identifying K rather than an I.

The deleted word before the next-line limite retains an initial upright l and a high terminal loop/angled stroke, but a thick descending cancellation covers its medial letters and dot positions. The surviving strokes do not establish the entire word.

P and the raised minus-one are clear, followed by an opening parenthesis. Reinspection confirms the first interval bracket has its curved upright on the left and both tips on the right: [. A heavy horizontal strike covers the interval content; short lower strokes and a loop survive, but their full values and order cannot be certified from this view. The final left bracket and closing parenthesis are visible. The bracket direction is resolved while the contents remain uncertain.

In the crossed abbreviation before fermé, a long looped f descends below the cancellation, a second tall narrow loop remains above it, and a short final upright/hook survives to the right. These are the compact fblt strokes also present in the following uncancelled occurrence.

The uncancelled abbreviation at the left of the next line has a long descending f, a tall joined middle stroke returning to a short bowl, and a separate short hooked final t. The word is separated by a visible gap from the following fermé.

The opening has an upright loop compatible with D and a lower descending stroke farther right, but thick horizontal cancellation and a large return loop intersect the middle letters. The accent and full après sequence cannot be separated securely.

Between the opening word and the surname phrase, a tall stem and a small upward turn survive, while the short intervening strokes coincide with the cancellation line. They do not distinguish a complete pair of words.

A tall initial B-like two-part form, a short separating dash, and a later rounded capital D survive. Much of the intervening name lies on the strikeout; its inner letters and terminal accent cannot be verified in full. The preceding de is also crossed at x-height.

At the far right, two stems enclose an upper triangular white area and are connected by a sloping crossbar. This is the capital A, with its lower right stem continuing below the crossbar despite nearby deletion strokes.

The continuation is nearly coincident with a thick horizontal erasure. Only isolated small humps above it remain; the large descending and returning line crossing the same area cannot safely be assigned to a letter. No complete word boundary or pair is recoverable.

The initial Il is buried where the enclosing oval and vertical cancellation meet. To its right, the paired tall f strokes, detached i dot and short t identify suffit; a d ascent follows, then prouver begins with a distinct p descender and ends in the low joined trailing strokes. Uncertainty can be restricted to Il.

The first word starts with the long q descender below the strike and retains the short joined ue exit. After a gap, the second word starts with a small s hook and continues in the low ur stroke; these lower strokes remain visible beneath the cancellation.

The two t uprights bracketing the low ou strokes and the final e-shaped exit support toute. The next group has a low run and a rising loop, but the cancellation covers the upper bodies and prevents secure identification of the initial p and the whole ending of partie.

Following the tentative partie group, low scalloped remnants lie under a continuous strikeout. Their exact boundary with the following proposed de and tout is obscured, and no complete additional word is visible.

In the heavily crossed interval before the rightmost upright cluster, a short low tail and rounded remnants survive. Neither an isolated d bowl with its ascender nor a separate complete de can be assigned securely; adjacent word boundaries are buried.

The rightmost cluster has an upright loop and small low return strokes, crossed by both diagonal and horizontal deletion. These remnants do not distinguish a full t-ou-t sequence; the proposed position also depends on obscured preceding boundaries.

At the beginning of the next line, most of the low letter bodies merge with the thick erasure. A slanted higher stroke and a small low ending remain, but the initial ens- and middle -emb- are not separately visible enough to confirm ensemble.

The assigned area has a tall crossed f-like stroke with a descending loop near x610. The long horizontal cancellation absorbs the following small letters almost completely; a short upper tick survives near the end but cannot establish the full r-m-é sequence. The preceding source-word boundaries are also obscured.

Immediately before the displayed L∞(K), a short upright d ascender protrudes above the cancellation line and returns into a low rightward e-like stroke. The two-letter group is separated from the following capital L.

After L∞(K), the small est group survives below the rule as a shallow initial curve and an angular final upward turn. The following abbreviation has a long descending f stroke, a rising joined middle stem and a short upright final component, visibly the same compressed fblt form as the clear occurrence farther down.

Two groups follow the fblt abbreviation. The first has an open c-like beginning, a midword descending loop and a later short tall stroke, suggesting compact, but its baseline and most small letters coincide with a heavy cancellation. The final group has a conspicuous tall looped f and some connected low humps; the purported accent and intervening letters are crossed, so fermé must also remain uncertain.

Below the inserted words, the deleted line retains a short curved et group, a clear descending p at the start of par, and the longer conséquent group with its q descender and short terminal group. The horizontal deletion crosses the small connecting letters but does not remove these principal strokes.

The phrase begins with the low connected strokes of une, followed by suite with a long low body and raised central crossing. Bornée begins with a looped b ascender and ends in the accented final e group; there is no separate final s after either suite or bornée.

The word begins with a separate open c, connected low strokes, and a clear long g descender. Its ending runs into a raised triangular return. That compressed terminal turn resembles the page’s final t in tendant, but it does not separately expose an n and t, so the ending cannot reliably distinguish converge from convergent.

Before fermé, the abbreviation has a deep looped f stroke, a joined high middle stem and a short separate final upright hook. It is compressed to the same three visible components as the repeated fblt below.

Three separated abbreviation groups are visible: the first has the tall descending f and compact final hook; the middle has a low r/e beginning, a high l arch and a separate crossed t; the last has an open c, a p descender and a rising final t stroke.

On renewed inspection, the superscript has a short upper-left flag feeding a single thick descending stem. The bottom is rounded, with only a small local turn rather than a diagonal descent into an extended horizontal foot. Those visible features support 1 despite the ink being thicker than the simple 1 below.

Under the heavy strikeout, the initial d remains visible as a rounded loop with a tall upright, followed by low connected o/n strokes and a short right terminal c-like curl. The crossing does not extend to create an additional word.

Inside the final parentheses the letter is narrow, with a short nearly vertical stem and two small right arms attached low on it. It lacks the tall broad upper-right diagonal of the capital K in the immediately preceding L^1(K), supporting the listed lower-case k.
